newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB down sharply in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB down sharply in heavy trade.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Plc dropped in heavy trade on Wednesday amid signs of intensifying domestic competition and as the sector succumbed to interest rate fears, dealers and analysts said.
Lloyds shares were down 16p or three percent at 497-1/2 by 1553 GMT in volume of 19 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the UK market.
Abbey National Plc, also heavily exposed to the UK mortgage and savings market, was also down sharply to be 15-1/2p lower at 734 in volume of 1.8 million.
Among other bank stocks, Barclays Plc was down 15p at 10.82-1/2, National Westminster Bank Plc was down 7p at 704-1/2 and Bank of Scotland Plc was down 6p at 340-1/2.

Dealers and analysts said there was no single reason for the particular weakness in Lloyds and Abbey but highlighted a statement by mutually-owned Bradford & Bingley Building Society increase in savings rates.
"Maybe that has highlighted what people already knew about competition and pressure on margins," said Ian Poulter, analyst at Williams de Broe.

Poulter also pointed out that bank stocks had been hit on both sides of the Atlantic by speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates at next week's meeting of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy committee.
Anyway, after sharp gains in UK bank stocks this year, there is plenty of scope for profit-taking in the sector's leading shares.
Lloyds hit a record 538p on March 5, up 25 percent on its level at the end of last year, and other bank shares have also risen sharply in recent months.
